findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no topic_users row
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can legitimately return nil: users in mailing-list mode receive notification emails for topics they have never visited (the mailer itself handles this — `TopicUser.get` is used nil-tolerantly in send_notification_email), as do users emailed via a topic invite. The very next lines dereference `tu.notification_level`, so clicking the new per-topic unsubscribe link from such an email raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should handle the missing row, e.g. by creating it via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])`.

findings.title: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe mutates state with no token or confirmation
findings.body: The new unsubscribe endpoint is a plain GET route that immediately changes the user's topic notification_level before rendering any page. Because GET requests carry no CSRF token, any third-party page that causes a logged-in user's browser to request the URL (e.g., an embedded pointing at the unsubscribe link) can silently mute or downgrade that user's subscription. Additionally, antivirus link scanners and browser/email prefetchers that fetch links from incoming mail will unsubscribe users without them ever clicking anything. State-changing actions should require POST, or the link should land on a confirmation page / use a signed token like the digest unsubscribe key.

findings.title: Unsubscribe downgrades watching/tracking users to 'regular', contradicting the 'stop notifications' copy
findings.body: For users whose notification_level is watching or tracking, the unsubscribe action sets the level to regular rather than muted. At 'regular' the user still receives notifications — and notification emails — whenever someone replies to them or mentions them in that topic. Yet the email link text says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the landing page says 'You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>'. Users who click the link will keep receiving emails for the topic, which is both a functional and messaging bug: either mute unconditionally or change the copy to say notifications are only reduced.

findings.title: Template path does not match the route name, so the unsubscribe UI will not render
findings.body: The client route is registered as a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe` in app-route-map.js.es6, and the controller and view are named `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, so Ember resolves the template for that route under the name 'topicUnsubscribe'. The template added here lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which registers as 'topic/unsubscribe' — a name only a child route `topic.unsubscribe` of the topic resource would look up. The route will therefore render with no template (or raise a missing-template error in development). Move the file to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs to match the route, controller, and view naming.

findings.title: No request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The only spec change in this PR adds an unsubscribe_url option to an existing message-builder test. There are no request specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering the notification-level transitions (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted), the behavior when the user has no topic_users row, or the slug-mismatch redirect. A request spec for the missing-row case would have caught the nil-dereference crash on the primary path of this feature.
